newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriot leader to meet U.N. chief in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriot leader to meet U.N. chief in Geneva.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan will meet Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash in Geneva next week, the U.N. resident envoy on the divided island said on Wednesday.

Denktash, head of the breakaway state in northern Cyprus recognised only by Ankara, is meeting the U.N. chief as an intensive round of consultations are underway for the resumption of direct talks between the two sides later this year.

"We are shooting (for talks) in the middle of the year and there is no specific date," chief of mission of U.N. forces in Cyprus, Gustave Feissel, told reporters after meeting with President Glafcos Clerides, the Greek Cypriot leader.
Feissel said he would give the secretary-general an "assessment of the way things are going" on the proximity talks, which started in early March.
Leaders of Cyprus's two communities, divided since Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974 after a coup sponsored by Athens, have not met since October 1994.

The United Nations, which has had a peacekeeping force stationed in Cyprus since 1963, and a small army of mediators have been trying for decades to reunite the island under a federal umbrella, without any noteworthy results.

The U.N. has indicated it wants to see both sides make "goodwill gestures" to the other to improve the climate for talks, soured after the killings of three Greek Cypriots on the ceasefire line by Turks or Turkish Cypriots, and the shooting of a Turkish Cypriot sentry between August and October last year.
Feissel refused to specify what the U.N. expected from the two sides.
The U.N. have a force of 1,200, patrolling a buffer zone between some 30,000 mainland Turkish forces in northern Cyprus and 11,500 Greek Cypriot conscripts in the south.
Incidents between the two sides have dropped considerably in recent weeks.

"For the past two weeks UNFICYP (United Nations Forces in Cyprus) has noticed a drop in the number of (military) incidents on a daily basis," spokesman Waldemar Rokoszewski said. "The conclusion is both sides are showing much more restraint than in previous months."
